name: Tendril Climb
desc: A creeper hunting its way up a trellis and never finishing — free apices circumnutate in live searching sweeps until a tendril finds a batten and coils onto it, the stem zigzags up the support shedding fluttering leaves, and old growth dries to gold and is pruned so a new shoot can take the freed lattice; a pool of eighteen staggered generations, so something is always germinating, always racing, always senescing.

energy.doc: wind/flutter amplitude + how wildly the free apices circumnutate + growth rate (master knob)

density.doc: how many vines of the 18-stem pool are on the trellis (2 at 0 -> 12 at 1)

scale.doc: trellis pitch and leaf/stem size vs frame (2.4 = coarse, huge foliage)

hue.doc: foliage hue (also tones the cyanotype ground)

x.doc: trellis pattern anchor across the frame

y.doc: trellis pattern anchor down the frame

leafiness.doc: node spacing + leaf size — bare whips at 0, a dense climbing mass at 1

trellis.doc: support geometry the vine has to find and follow

style.doc: aesthetic — toned plate w/ ink line + wash; Atkins photogram (pale mass on Prussian blue, no line); additive translucent radiograph; flat dark mass on a graded warm ground

seed.doc: seeds the trellis jitter, germination points and every growth decision

alpha.doc: opacity of the plant over its trellis
